To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The new pair of palladium complexes Pd4 and PD5 ligated with N-(5, 6, 7-trihydroquino-lin-8-ylidine)arylamine ligand have been prepared and characterized.

the new palladium complexes Pd4 andPd5 ligated with N-(5, 6, 7-trihydro-quinolin-8ylidene)arylamines are highly active catalysts in methyl acrylatae (MA) polymerizations as well as methyl aerylatae/norbornene copolymerizations.

the geometry of Pd4, Pd5 and Pd6 complexes is slightly distorted square plan, the Pd4 and the Pd5 complexes are highly active catalysts in the methyl acrylate polymerization and methyl acrylate-co-norbornene copolymerization and the Pd4 complex is a highly active catalyst in the coupling reactions of haloarenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and synthesis of new palladium complexes with constrained N-(8-ylidenerhodoquinoline) ligands and their catalytic applications in MA polymerization, MA/NB copolymerization as well as Heck coupling.
the development of new constrained ligands for palladium-catalyzed reactions, such as Heck coupling, MA polymerization and MA/NB copolymerization.
the development of a novel family of constrained N-(5-6-7-trihydroquionolin-8-ylene)arylamine ligand and its palladium complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the geometry constrained N-(5.6.7-trihydroquinaldin-8-ylidine)arylamine ligand is able to efficiently mediating the polymerization of MA, copolymerization of MA and NB as well as Heck coupling.
the geometry constrained palladium complexes are highly efficient catalyst in MA polymerization as well in MA/NB copolymerization and also in the Heck coupling of haloarene with styrene.
these palladium complexes are promising catalysts in MA polymerization and MA/NB copolymerization, as well as in C–C bond formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these palladium complexes are good catalyst candidates in MA polymerization and Heck reaction.
the introduction of the constrained ligands to the palladium complexes can not only improve the activity of MA polymerization but also increase the catalytic efficiency of Heck reactions.
the constrained N-(5-6,7-triquinolin-8-yleidene)aryl-amine ligands can be considered as a new class of ligands for the palladium catalysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometry-constrained ligands are able to provide the palladium complexes with high activity toward the polymerization of MA and MA/NB copolymerization as well as the Heck coupling reaction.
the geometry of the palladium complexes is an important parameter in determining the catalytic performance.
the constrained geometry of ligands can be used as a powerful tool to design highly efficient and robust catalysts.
